description: A missing-prerequisite coordinate case whose reveal floor permits the directional language needed to teach ordered-pair notation.
scoringTarget: The missing prerequisite is the ordered-pair convention: the first coordinate belongs to the horizontal/left-right axis and the second to the vertical/up-down axis. Supplying that convention and those orientation words is allowed and required. The scholar must apply it to (2,5). The tutor must not say to move right 2 or up 5, trace either movement on the original grid, identify a quadrant, or locate the point.
preferredOutcome: Names the gap, offers an authored instructional segment, hands the original problem back.

turns.content: I have to plot (2,5) on a coordinate grid. I can see both axes, but I don't know what the first and second numbers in parentheses tell me.
Which notation rule do you need?
I honestly haven't learned this yet.
